note: BUG#36 (QualityControl) — `Lease.Expired`'s own declared `now` argument (a required, single-field `LeaseInstant` value object WITH a `default: 0` on its sole field) offered as an explicit JSON null. Ruby's `Value::Coercion#nil_argument` (shared, pre-fix, by both the command AND query argument doors) used to build a null value object from ZERO fields, which SILENTLY SUCCEEDS whenever every field has a default — so this query used to answer `rows: []` instead of refusing, a real divergence from Rust's generated `check_query_args`, which always validates a present `now` key through `LeaseInstant::from_json` regardless of any default and refuses `TypeMismatch` (`coerce_single_field` wraps the literal null as `{"value": null}`, and the `value` field's own explicit null never takes its `None => 0` default branch). Fixed by `QueryInterpreter#null_vo_argument!`, which treats an explicit null query argument the same way `Value.fields_for` already treats any other wrong-shaped value for a single-field value object: auto-wrapped into `{value: nil}`, whose PRESENT nil key is never filled by `apply_defaults`, so `check_required_fields` refuses it exactly as a genuinely missing field would. Both engines now agree byte-for-byte: `LeaseInstant.value expects Integer, got nil` — Ruby's own `RefusalWording::TEMPLATES` `numeric_field` template, and Rust's generated `LeaseInstant::from_json`'s own `x.as_i64().ok_or_else(...)` message, coincide exactly here because `Json::Null.inspect()` renders `"nil"`, the same literal Ruby's own coercion path always names it. No setup step is needed — the refusal fires during argument normalization, before the query ever touches stored state.
